A: Your visa allocation quota unlocks ΓÇö each license comes with a set number of eligible, exclusive visa slots you can use to sponsor employees.

Q: How do I bring employees onto my visa quota?
A: Once your quota is active, you can sponsor employees under your company at Meydan Free Zone regardless of your business activity (e.g., a cargo loading and unloading business or a consultancy). Meydan Free Zone supports the full process, including medicals, Emirates ID, and visa stamping, to keep you compliant with Dubai labour law.

Q: Do I need an NOC from a previous employer to sponsor or switch visas?
A: No ΓÇö no NOC (No Objection Certificate) is needed from a previous employer to sponsor yourself or your team under a Meydan Free Zone license.

Q: What does the mandatory medical fitness test involve?
A: After arriving in the UAE, applicants must complete a medical fitness test at an approved health centre. This typically includes a blood test and a chest X-ray, used to screen for certain communicable diseases as required for UAE residency.

Q: What happens if I don't pass the medical fitness test?
A: Failing the fitness test (for example, due to certain communicable diseases) will lead to the visa application being rejected. This is a standard UAE government requirement and not specific to Meydan Free Zone.

Q: What is involved in Emirates ID biometric registration?
A: Biometric registration involves submitting fingerprints and a facial scan at an ICP-approved centre, alongside your passport-style photo. This data is linked directly to your visa and Emirates ID application.

Q: How long do the medical test and biometric steps typically take?
A: Results and biometric appointment coordination generally take around 5ΓÇô7 working days through the normal service, followed by a further 3ΓÇô5 working days for visa stamping and Emirates ID issuance ΓÇö though timelines can vary based on appointment availability.

Q: Do I need to attend the medical and biometric appointments in person?
A: Yes, both the medical fitness test and biometric enrolment (fingerprint and facial scan) require physical attendance at a designated, government-approved centre ΓÇö these cannot be completed remotely.

Q: Is there a difference in the medical/biometric process depending on whether I'm inside or outside the UAE when I apply?
A: Yes.

Inside-country process: For individuals already in the UAE (often on a tourist visa) who are changing visa status, or whose previous visa was cancelled. Medical and biometric steps are completed inside the country as part of the status change.

Outside-country process: For individuals currently outside the UAE. They enter on an entry permit/e-visa, and the medical and biometric appointments are scheduled and completed once they arrive inside the UAE

Q: Is a VIP or fast-track option available for medical and biometric appointments?
A: Yes. Arnifi can assist with VIP fast-track upgrades where available, helping reduce waiting times for medical coordination, biometric appointments, application tracking, and Emirates ID collection

Q: What does the VIP fast-track process typically involve?
A: A fast-track option can significantly cut down waiting time and schedule a priority biometric appointment at a nearby authorised Government Services Centre, often within a short window of arrival ΓÇö compared to standard queue-based booking.

Q: Who should consider the VIP fast-track option?
A: It's best suited to founders and employees who need their Emirates ID or visa urgently ΓÇö for example, ahead of travel, a bank account application, or a work start date ΓÇö and want to avoid standard appointment wait times.

Q: Does choosing VIP fast-track change the underlying steps required?
A: No ΓÇö the mandatory steps (medical fitness test, biometric enrolment, ICP processing) remain the same. The VIP option primarily changes appointment priority and waiting time, not the requirements themselves.

Q: How quickly can the process be completed with full support?
A: With coordinated support, most Emirates ID applications can be completed in as little as 2 business days once medical and biometric steps are cleared, though overall visa timelines depend on entry permit, quota, and stamping stages as well.

Q: How are medical and biometric appointments scheduled?
A: Once the entry permit (or in-country status change) is issued, Arnifi books both the medical fitness test appointment and the biometric/Emirates ID appointment on the applicant's behalf. The applicant doesn't need to book anything themselves ΓÇö they're simply informed of the date, time, and centre once it's confirmed. You'll also receive an SMS from ICP once the appointment is created in the system.

Q: Which centres are used for the medical fitness test?
A: Medical fitness appointments are booked at one of the government-approved medical fitness centres across Dubai. Standard (non-VIP) centres include Al Muhaisnah, Al Lusaily, Al Quoz, Al Yalayis Jabal Ali, SalemΓÇôDAFZA, Al Garhoud, Abu Hail, SalemΓÇôAl Muhaisnah, SalemΓÇôAl Rashidiya, SalemΓÇôAXS, SalemΓÇôDIFC, SalemΓÇôEmirates, SalemΓÇôJAFZA, SalemΓÇôAl Karama, SalemΓÇôAl Nahda, SalemΓÇôAl Yalayis DIP, SalemΓÇôBur Dubai, SalemΓÇôDubai Airport (airport staff renewals only), SalemΓÇôENOC, SalemΓÇôZaabeel, and SalemΓÇôJVC..

Q: What are the working hours at the standard medical centres?
A: Hours vary by centre ΓÇö most run MondayΓÇôThursday roughly 7:00/7:30 AM to 3:30 PM (some until 10:00 PM), with shorter Friday hours (typically 7:30 AMΓÇô12:00 PM). Several centres run extended or 24/7 hours, including Al Yalayis Jabal Ali, Abu Hail, and SalemΓÇôAl Muhaisnah (24/7, closed 12:00ΓÇô2:00 PM Fridays for prayers), while Al Quoz, SalemΓÇôAl Karama, and SalemΓÇôBur Dubai run 7 days a week from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM. Confirm exact timing for your assigned centre once booked, since hours can change.

Q: Are there dedicated VIP medical fitness centres?
A: Yes ΓÇö Dubai Knowledge Park, City Walk, and Index, which offer longer daily hours (many open until 10:00 PM on weekdays, plus Saturday/Sunday hours) to support faster, priority processing.

Q: Where are the biometric (Emirates ID) appointments conducted?
A: At one of ICP's Customer Happiness Centres: Al Barsha (near Saudi German Hospital), Alghazal (Al Bida area, Al Ghazal Mall), Al Rashidiya (behind Rashidiya Council, opposite Mohammed Noor Boys School), Al Nahda (inside Salem Medical Examination Centre, Al Qusais), Alyalyis (Dubai Investments Park 2), Al Baraha (Deira, inside Al Baraha Smart Medical Fitness Center for Residency), and Hatta Customer Happiness Office.

Q: Is a VIP or fast-track option available for medical and biometric appointments?
A: Yes. Applicants can opt for the VIP process for an additional AED 2,000 on top of standard fees. With VIP, both the medical fitness test and the biometric appointment can be arranged on the same day, significantly cutting down overall waiting time versus the standard process

Q: Where do VIP medical appointments take place?
A: At the designated VIP centres ΓÇö Dubai Knowledge Park, City Walk, or Index tower ΓÇö rather than the standard medical centres.

Q: Where do VIP biometric appointments take place?
A: Applicants must visit the Al Yalayis Customer Happiness Center specifically to complete the VIP biometric appointment.

Q: Can the medical and biometric steps really be completed on the same day with VIP?
A: Yes ΓÇö that's the core benefit. Instead of falling on separate days as with the standard process, VIP allows both to be scheduled and completed the same day, speeding up the overall visa timeline.

Q: Who should consider the VIP fast-track option?
A: Applicants who need their Emirates ID or visa urgently ΓÇö ahead of travel, a bank account application, or a work start date ΓÇö and want to avoid standard wait times and the delay of separate medical/biometric visits

Q: Does choosing VIP fast-track change the underlying steps required?
A: No ΓÇö the mandatory steps (medical fitness test, biometric enrolment, ICP processing) stay the same. VIP changes the centre, appointment priority, and same-day scheduling, not the requirements themselves.

Q: What documents are required to request an increase in my company's visa quota allocation?
A: Five documents are needed: a Justification Letter, a Service Staff Agreement, a Designation List, the company's Business Plan, and a Lease Agreement.

Q: What should the Justification Letter include?
A: It must clearly state the company's current visa quota, the additional quota being requested, and the reason/justification for the increase.

Q: What is a Service Staff Agreement and what should it contain?
A: It specifies the number of employees to be added and the designation of each employee, and must be duly signed and stamped by the company's General Manager.

Q: What details must the Designation List include?
A: The current available visa quota, the number of additional slots required, and per-employee details ΓÇö Name, Nationality, Passport Number, and Designation ΓÇö also signed and stamped by the General Manager.

Q: What does the Company's Business Plan document need to cover?
A: For Arnifi Manpower: employee onboarding (digital contracts, KYC, documentation), lifecycle management (hiring to exit on one platform), payroll/WPS compliance, and multi-country workforce deployment.

Q: What must the Lease Agreement document specify for a quota increase request?
A: The company's agreement details, a description of the agreement, and its terms andconditions.

sections.introduction:
The UAE Golden Visa allows eligible residents to sponsor certain family members for long-term residence in the country. The Golden Dependent Visa provides a route for eligible dependants, including children, to obtain residence under the sponsorΓÇÖs Golden Visa.

The process involves checking the family visa eligibility, preparing sponsor and dependant documents, submitting the dependant application, completing verification and approval, and fulfilling medical, insurance, and Emirates ID requirements where applicable. The dependantΓÇÖs residence visa is linked to the sponsorΓÇÖs own visa validity.

There are also specific rules depending on the dependantΓÇÖs relationship and age. Daughters can be sponsored as long as they remain unmarried, while sons may have different age-based conditions. The process also requires the dependant to be physically present in the UAE for the applicable stages. Arnifi assists with the application journey, document preparation, verification, medical and insurance coordination, and Emirates ID formalities.
sections.highlights_and_benefits:
Long-Term Family Residency
Eligible dependants can receive residence for the same number of years as the sponsorΓÇÖs own visa.

10-Year Visa Validity
Eligible family sponsorship can provide residence for up to 10 years, depending on the sponsorΓÇÖs visa validity.

Family Sponsorship
Golden Visa holders can sponsor eligible family members under the applicable UAE family residence framework.

Support for Stepchildren
Stepchildren can be sponsored under a 10-year Family Visa, subject to applicable requirements.

Flexible Daughter Sponsorship

Structured Application Process
The process covers application submission, verification, medical requirements, residence visa issuance, biometrics, and Emirates ID delivery.

Arnifi Assistance
Arnifi supports the application process, including document coordination, submission, verification, medical and insurance processing, and Emirates ID procedures.
sections.process_flow:
1. Family Visa Document Collection: Share all the required family visa documents with the Arnifi team for review and processing.

2. Dependent Visa Application: Once the documents are received, our team will initiate the dependent visa application with the relevant authorities.

3. Verification & Approval: DLD Cube will verify the sponsorΓÇÖs and dependentΓÇÖs documents. Once the application is approved, Arnifi will share the status update and proceed with the next steps.

4. Medical Examination & Insurance: Complete the dependentΓÇÖs medical fitness examination and arrange the required health insurance. Medical results are typically available within approximately 30 minutes.

5. Residence Visa Issuance: Following GDRFA approval, the dependentΓÇÖs electronic residence visa (e-Visa) will be issued.

6. Biometrics & Emirates ID: Complete the Emirates ID biometric process. Once completed, the Emirates ID card will be printed and delivered to the registered address.
sections.faqs:
Q: How long is a Golden Dependent Visa valid?
A: The dependant receives the same number of years as the sponsorΓÇÖs own visa, subject to applicable eligibility rules.

Q: Can stepchildren be sponsored under a Golden Dependent Visa?
A: Yes. A stepchild can be sponsored under a 10-year Family Visa.

Q: Can daughters be sponsored after reaching adulthood?
A: Yes. Daughters can be sponsored at any age as long as they remain unmarried.

Q: What happens when a dependantΓÇÖs visa expires?
A: A 30-day grace period is available after visa expiry to complete renewal before fines apply

Q: Does the dependant need to be physically present in the UAE?
A: Yes. Physical presence is required throughout the applicable process for the dependant application.

Q: How quickly are medical results available?
A: The medical examination results are typically available within approximately 30 minutes, according to the provided process information.

Q: How many years is the Golden Dependent Visa valid for?
A: The dependent visa is issued for the same number of years as the sponsor's own visa. For
example, a sponsor holding a 10-year Investor Visa can sponsor a dependent for 10 years; a
2-year or 5-year sponsor visa gives a matching 2-year or 5-year dependent visa.

Q: Who can sponsor a dependent under the DLD Cube Golden Visa?
A: Property investor visa holders (2, 5, or 10-year visas) and 5-year retiree visa holders can
sponsor eligible dependents, provided their own visa is valid and in good standing.

Q: Who can be sponsored as a dependent?
A: Spouse (husband or wife), children (sons and daughters, including stepchildren), and ΓÇö
where the sponsor is a son or daughter who already holds a Golden Visa ΓÇö their parents.

Q: What are the benefits of the Golden Family/Dependent Visa?
A: It lets sponsors keep their spouse and children in the same country for the full duration of
the sponsor's visa, allows dependents to stay outside the UAE for up to 6 months without the
visa being cancelled, and ΓÇö for the 10-year visa ΓÇö doesn't require renewal every two years like
other categories.

Q: Are all nationalities eligible to apply?
A: Yes, visitors of all nationalities can apply for a family visa in the UAE under this Golden
Visa programme.

Q: What sponsor details are required on the application form?
A: The sponsor's full name, email ID, UAE mobile number (+971, OTP-verified), passport
number, visa number, and a copy of the sponsor's visa.

Q: What documents are required from the sponsor?
A: The sponsor's passport and residence visa copies. If the mother is the sponsor, a
notarized NOC letter from the father is also required for boys under 18 and girls under 21. If the
father is the sponsor, proof of the mother's status (her residence visa or Emirates ID copy) is
required.

Q: What documents are required for a dependent child?
A: A clear colour passport copy (valid more than 6 months), the previous residence visa copy
if applicable, a legalized birth certificate (attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UAE
Embassy, then Arabic-translated), and a high-quality digital photo matching ICP specifications.
Applicants from Iran, Pakistan, Iraq, Libya, or Afghanistan must also provide a National ID.

Q: What if the child's birth certificate isn't available?
A: A letter from the consulate can be used instead, provided it is attested by MOFA,
translated into Arabic, and begins with the wording ΓÇ£This is to confirmΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£This is to clarify.ΓÇ¥

Q: What documents are required for a spouse (husband/wife)?
A: A marriage certificate legalized by MOFA and the UAE Embassy, then Arabic-translated ΓÇö
or, if unavailable, a consulate letter using the same ΓÇ£confirm/clarifyΓÇ¥ wording. National ID is also
required for applicants from Iran, Pakistan, Iraq, Libya, or Afghanistan.

Q: Is there a special rule for consulate letters confirming a dependent's relationship?
A: Yes ΓÇö the letter must mention both the mother's and the father's names in the same letter.
Letters that omit either parent's name will not be approved.

Q: What is the age rule for sponsoring a son?
A: Under a 2-year sponsor visa, boys are entitled to 2-year visa increments (instead of 1) until
they turn 25. They become ineligible for renewal after age 25.

Q: What is the age rule for sponsoring a daughter?
A: There is no age limit for sponsoring a daughter, as long as she remains unmarried.

Q: Is there an extra step for a son or daughter over 18?
A: Yes ΓÇö a son or daughter over 18 must sign the unmarried undertaking letter online, at the
time the dependent application is submitted.

Q: Can a stepchild be sponsored?
A: Yes, a stepchild can be sponsored under the 10-year Golden Visa.

Q: Can I sponsor my parents?
A: Yes ΓÇö a son or daughter who already holds a Golden Visa can sponsor their parents. This
option is reflected in the ΓÇ£SonΓÇ¥ / ΓÇ£DaughterΓÇ¥ choices on the ΓÇ£Who is Sponsor?ΓÇ¥ dropdown.

Q: Is medical insurance mandatory for the dependent?
A: Yes. As per GDRFA regulation, medical insurance is compulsory for every residence
permit application. DLD Cube can assist with registering either DHA Basic Insurance or
Comprehensive Insurance for the sponsor and family.

Q: Can someone else attend the DLD Cube Centre on the applicant's behalf?
A: No. Only the applicant is permitted entry to the DLD Cube Centre; applications submitted
by other parties are not accepted.

Q: Can a dependent visa be applied for while the applicant is outside the UAE?
A: No. Physical presence inside the UAE is required throughout the residency proceedings,
and travel is not permitted mid-process.

Q: What happens once the documents are verified?
A: An approval email is issued together with the government payment link, which is payable
only through the official portal link.

Q: What happens during the medical examination step?
A: A Fitness Test Application email confirms the medical appointment; the fee is already paid,
so no extra charge is due at the centre. The dependent can visit any approved medical centre ΓÇö
such as Smart Salem City Walk, DIFC Index Tower, or Dubai Knowledge Park ΓÇö and must carry
the original passport for a blood test and X-ray.

Q: How long does the medical result take?
A: Results are typically received by email/SMS within about 30 minutes of completing the
test. If the dependent does not pass, DHA will notify them directly to schedule a retake.

Q: How will I know the visa's status while it's being processed?
A: A ΓÇ£Status NotificationΓÇ¥ email lists each process line item ΓÇö such as DLD approval fees,
medical, GDRFA residency, Emirates ID application, and medical insurance ΓÇö and its current
status. Updates are sent by email; there's no need to visit the centre for status checks.

Q: What happens once the residence visa is approved?
A: GDRFA issues the electronic Dependent Visa (e-Visa). An email confirms it is ready and
attaches a copy, along with the Emirates ID application form.

Q: Is biometric enrollment always required?
A: Only if the dependent does not already hold an Emirates ID. In that case, they must visit
one of the listed EID service centres ΓÇö Al Barsha, Al Yalayais, Al Ghazal, or Al Nahda ΓÇö for
fingerprinting and an eye/iris scan, carrying the original passport, medical results, and the EID
application form.

Q: How is the Emirates ID delivered?
A: The Zajel courier contacts the applicant to arrange delivery to the same address given
during the visa application. The card is typically delivered within 1ΓÇô2 working days of biometrics.

Q: When is the dependent visa process considered complete?
A: When the electronic Dependent Visa has been issued, Emirates ID biometrics are
completed, the physical Emirates ID card has been delivered, and all documents and records
are updated in the system.

Q: What is the grace period if the dependent visa expires?
A: Residents are given a 30-day grace period after expiry to renew the visa before fines
apply.

sections.faqs:
Q: What are the standard corporate tax rates in Hong Kong?
A: Hong Kong utilizes a two-tiered profits tax regime where the first HKD 2 million of assessable corporate profits are taxed at a low rate of 8.25%, with any remaining profits exceeding that threshold subject to a standard rate of 16.5%.

Q: When is a Hong Kong company required to file its first Profits Tax Return?
A: The Inland Revenue Department typically issues a newly incorporated entity its first formal Profits Tax Return approximately 18 months following the official date of incorporation.

Q: Is an independent audit mandatory prior to filing a Profits Tax Return?
A: Yes. Under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance, actively trading companies must append their Profits Tax Return with financial statements audited by an independent, licensed Hong Kong CPA. Legally dormant companies are exempt from this requirement.

Q: What is the IRD iXBRL data filing requirement?
A: The IRD is implementing digital tax filing in a phased manner via the eTax portal. Utilizing the specialized iXBRL electronic data format is mandatory for in-scope multinational enterprise (MNE) groups, with requirements progressively expanding toward a target of full mandatory electronic filing for all Hong Kong businesses by 2030.

Q: Does Hong Kong tax income earned outside its borders?
A: Generally, no. Hong Kong operates on a territorial taxation basis for active trade profits. However, under the Foreign Sourced Income Exemption (FSIE) regime, certain foreign-sourced passive income (such as dividends, interest, and disposal gains) is subject to Profits Tax unless specific economic substance or nexus requirements are met.

sections.faqs:
Q: Are all Hong Kong companies required to perform an annual statutory audit?
A: Yes. All active companies incorporated under the Companies Ordinance must undergo an annual statutory audit. Only companies that have passed a special resolution and formally declared their dormant status with the Companies Registry are exempt.

Q: Who is authorized to conduct a statutory audit in Hong Kong?
A: Statutory audits must be performed exclusively by an independent, external Certified Public Accountant (CPA) holding a valid practicing certificate from the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council (AFRC).

Q: What is the statutory deadline for filing audited accounts?
A: Present at the AGM within 9 months of the year-end (6 months for public companies) and submit to the IRD with the Profits Tax Return.

Q: Can a company use simplified accounting standards for an audit?
A: Yes. Private companies that satisfy at least two of the three statutory size criteria (annual revenue Γëñ HKD 100 million, total assets Γëñ HKD 100 million, and employees Γëñ 100) can opt for the simplified Small and Medium-Sized Entity Financial Reporting Standard (SME-FRS).

Q: What is the role of the AFRC in Hong Kong audits?
A: The Accounting and Financial Reporting Council (AFRC) is the independent statutory regulatory body tasked with supervising the CPA profession, enforcing audit quality, and protecting investor interests.

sections.introduction:
Corporate Tax Registration in UAE is the process through which eligible UAE businesses register with the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) for Corporate Tax and complete their applicable tax compliance requirements. Corporate Tax is charged at 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, while taxable income up to AED 375,000 is subject to the applicable 0% rate.

The registration process is completed through the EmaraTax portal and involves creating the company's account, preparing and submitting the Corporate Tax application, and completing any verification requirements requested by the FTA. Corporate Tax filing is mandatory for businesses with a filing obligation, even where there is no tax payable.

Arnifi supports businesses throughout the Corporate Tax Registration in UAE process, from account creation and OTP verification to application submission, FTA verification, and final approval. The Corporate Tax return is generally due within 9 months from the end of the relevant financial year, with a 30 September deadline where the financial year ends on 31 December.

sections.faqs:
Q: What is Corporate Tax Registration in UAE?
A: Corporate Tax Registration in UAE is the process of registering an eligible business with the Federal Tax Authority for Corporate Tax purposes.

Q: Who must register for Corporate Tax in the UAE?
A: All Taxable Persons must register for Corporate Tax and obtain a Tax Registration Number, regardless of whether they ultimately have a final tax liability.

Q: What is the Corporate Tax rate in the UAE?
A: The standard rate is 9% on taxable income exceeding AED 375,000. Taxable income up to AED 375,000 is subject to a 0% rate

Q: When is the Corporate Tax return and payment due?
A: The return must be filed and the tax paid within nine months from the end of the relevant financial year. There are no advance quarterly payments.

Q: What is Small Business Relief?
A: Businesses with revenue not exceeding AED 3 million in a tax period may elect for Small Business Relief, treating them as having no taxable income. This is available for tax periods ending on or before 31 December 2026.

Q: Do Free Zone companies pay Corporate Tax?
A: Qualifying Free Zone Persons benefit from a 0% rate on Qualifying Income if they maintain adequate substance, comply with transfer pricing rules, and prepare audited financial statements. Non-qualifying income is taxed at 9%.

A: Generally, yes. Under Section 267 of the Companies Act 2016, active companies must have their accounts audited, though qualifying small private companies may opt for an exemption under SSM Practice Directive No. 10/2024.

Q: Who is authorized to conduct a statutory audit in Malaysia?
A: Statutory audits must be performed exclusively by an independent, external auditor licensed and approved by the Malaysian Ministry of Finance (MOF).

Q: What is the statutory deadline for lodging audited accounts with SSM?
A: Audited financial statements must be circulated to shareholders within six months of the financial year-end and officially lodged with SSM within 30 days after that circulation.

Q: Can Arnifi act as the company's statutory auditor?
A: No. Arnifi coordinates the pre-audit preparation and manages the accounting files, but the formal statutory audit must be executed by a separate, independent MOF-approved auditor.

Q: What accounting standards apply to private companies in Malaysia?
A: Most private SMEs in Malaysia utilize the simplified Malaysian Private Entities Reporting Standard (MPERS), while larger or public entities are required to use the full Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS).

sections.faqs:
Q: What is the standard corporate tax rate in Malaysia?
A: The standard corporate income tax rate in Malaysia is 24%. However, qualifying Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), defined as having paid-up capital of RM 2.5 million or less and gross business income not exceeding RM 50 million, benefit from a tiered preferential rate of 15% on the first RM 150,000 of chargeable income, 17% on the subsequent RM 150,001 to RM 600,000, and 24% on any remaining balance.

Q: When does SST registration become mandatory?
A: Registration for Sales and Service Tax (SST) is generally mandatory when a company's total taxable turnover for a 12-month period exceeds or is expected to exceed RM 500,000, though specific thresholds apply for certain regulated industries like F&B and professional services.

Q: When is the Malaysia corporate tax return (Form e-C) due?
A: Companies must submit their annual corporate tax return (Form e-C) to the LHDN no later than seven months following the close of their specific financial year-end.

Q: What is the CP204 requirement in Malaysia?
A: Form CP204 is a mandatory estimate of corporate tax payable to the LHDN. Existing companies (including dormant ones) must file it 30 days before their financial year begins. New companies have 3 months from starting operations, though qualifying new SMEs are exempt for their first two years

Q: Is e-Invoicing mandatory for companies in Malaysia?
A: Yes. The LHDN has mandated the phased implementation of e-Invoicing via the MyInvois portal.

Q: Can Arnifi act as the statutory auditor?

sections.introduction:
VAT Registration in UAE is the process through which a business registers with the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) to obtain a Tax Registration Number (TRN) and comply with UAE VAT requirements. The standard VAT rate in the UAE is 5% on applicable taxable supplies after a business becomes VAT registered.

VAT registration becomes mandatory when taxable supplies and imports exceed AED 375,000, while businesses may generally opt for voluntary registration once their taxable supplies, imports, or applicable taxable expenses exceed AED 187,500. Once registered, the business must charge VAT on applicable taxable supplies and meet its ongoing VAT filing and compliance obligations.
VAT returns are filed according to the tax period assigned by the FTA. Where a quarterly tax period applies, the VAT return is filed quarterly, with the return and any related payment generally due within 28 days from the end of the relevant tax period.

The VAT registration application is submitted through the FTA's EmaraTax platform. Arnifi assists with collecting and preparing the required documents, submitting the VAT registration application, responding to FTA verification requests, and following up until approval.

sections.faqs:
Q: What is VAT Registration in UAE?
A: VAT Registration in UAE is the process of registering an eligible business with the Federal Tax Authority to obtain a VAT Tax Registration Number (TRN).

Q: What is the VAT rate in the UAE?
A: The standard VAT rate in the UAE is 5% on applicable taxable supplies.

Q: When does a business start charging VAT?
A: Once a business is VAT registered, it generally charges VAT at the applicable rate on its taxable supplies and invoices, subject to the relevant UAE VAT rules.

Q: What is the mandatory VAT registration threshold in the UAE?
A: The mandatory threshold is AED 375,000 based on the value of taxable supplies and imports over the previous 12 months or expected in the next 30 days.

Q: What is the voluntary VAT registration threshold in the UAE?
A: The voluntary registration threshold is AED 187,500 based on taxable supplies, imports, or taxable expenses under the applicable rules.

Q: What documents are required for VAT Registration in UAE?
A: Documents generally include the trade licence, incorporation documents, identification documents, financial records, sales and purchase invoices, and other supporting documents required by the FTA.

Q: Where is the VAT registration application submitted?
A: VAT registration applications are submitted electronically through the FTA's EmaraTax platform.

Q: How long does VAT Registration in UAE take?
A: Arnifi's process includes 1~2 Business Days for document collection and drafting, 1 Business Day for registration, followed by FTA verification and approval.

Q: How often do I need to file VAT returns?
A: Businesses may be assigned different tax periods by the FTA. Where a quarterly tax period applies, VAT returns are filed quarterly.

Q: What is the VAT filing deadline in the UAE?
A: VAT returns and related payments are generally due within 28 days from the end of the relevant tax period.

sections.introduction: An Independent Contractor Agreement is a legal contract between a company and an external individual or entity engaged to provide specific services. Unlike an employment contract, it establishes that the contractor is self-employed and not entitled to employee benefits or protections. The agreement typically outlines the scope of work, project timelines, fees or payment terms, confidentiality obligations, intellectual property ownership, liability, and termination conditions. This document is crucial to clearly distinguish independent contractors from employees, as misclassification can result in tax, labor law, or social security liabilities for the hiring business. Contractors benefit from clarity on payment, project expectations, and rights over their work. Businesses gain flexibility in accessing specialized skills without the long-term obligations of employment. A well-drafted independent contractor agreement also ensures compliance with data protection, non-compete, and dispute resolution requirements. Without this agreement, both parties face risks of misunderstandings, unpaid work, or potential reclassification disputes. In todayΓÇÖs gig economy, such agreements are widely used across industries including IT, creative services, consulting, and engineering. A properly prepared document ensures professional accountability, legal clarity, and protection of both the contractor and the hiring entity.

Separates Employment Status
Clearly states that the contractor is not an employee, reducing misclassification risk.

Protects Intellectual Property

sections.introduction: A Promissory Note is a legally binding financial instrument in which one party promises in writing to pay a specific sum of money to another, either on demand or at a set future date. It typically includes key details such as the principal amount, interest rate, repayment schedule, maturity date, and conditions of default. Promissory notes are commonly used in loan arrangements between businesses, individuals, or financial institutions where formal loan agreements are unnecessary or impractical. A well-drafted promissory note creates a clear, enforceable obligation, reducing the risk of disputes and ensuring accountability. It also serves as evidence of debt that can be enforced in court if the borrower fails to repay. Depending on jurisdiction, promissory notes may need to be stamped or notarized to be legally valid. For lenders, the document provides legal protection and a straightforward remedy in case of default. For borrowers, it sets out clear repayment terms, avoiding uncertainty. Without a properly executed promissory note, lenders risk difficulty in enforcing repayment. Professional drafting ensures that the document complies with legal requirements while safeguarding the financial interests of both parties.

packages.package_name: Business Guide - E-Invoicing in the UAE

sections.introduction:
The UAE Ministry of Finance (MoF) and the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) are shifting business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-government (B2G) transactions to a fully digitized framework. Operating on a Decentralized Continuous Transaction Controls and Exchange (DCTCE) 5-corner model, this mandate requires corporate entities to replace traditional PDF billing with structured XML data routed exclusively through Accredited Service Providers (ASPs).

With a voluntary pilot phase opening on July 1, 2026, and mandatory enforcement for Phase 1 businesses starting January 1, 2027, companies face an immediate regulatory requirement to re-engineer financial architectures. This guide provides a detailed overview of the technical and compliance frameworks, decoding system mapping, and ASP onboarding rules to secure operational continuity and eliminate non-compliance penalties.
sections.highlights_and_benefits:
Implementation Timelines
A clear breakdown of Phase 1 deadlines, including the October 30, 2026, ASP appointment threshold and the mandatory January 1, 2027, go-live date.

Technical Demystification
A simplified overview of the Decentralized Continuous Transaction Controls and Exchange (DCTCE) 5-corner model, explaining how tax data routes to the FTA.

Data Structuring Rules
Step-by-step clarity on mandatory XML formats, Peppol PINT-AE specifications, and why standard PDF and paper invoices will no longer be legally recognized.

Scope And Exclusions
A precise look at which transactions fall under the mandate, specifically B2B and B2G, and which remain excluded, ensuring retail consumer (B2C) operations stay isolated.

Stay Penalty-Free
A comprehensive review of statutory data retention protocols and a breakdown of the AED 5,000 monthly administrative fines to keep the corporate entity secure.
sections.faqs:
Q: Are PDF invoices still legally valid in the UAE?
A: No. Once the mandate applies to a corporate entity, invoices must be generated and exchanged strictly as structured XML files.

Q: Which business transactions fall under this mandate?
A: The regulations apply strictly to all Business-to-Business (B2B) and Business-to-Government (B2G) transactions. Consumer retail sales (B2C) remain excluded.

Q: What is the specific deadline for Phase 1 companies?
A: Resident businesses with annual revenues hitting or exceeding AED 50 million must appoint an ASP by October 30, 2026, and go live by January 1, 2027.

Q: What is the penalty for missing the implementation timeline?
A: Failing to onboard an ASP and integrate the mandatory e-invoicing infrastructure triggers an administrative penalty of AED 5,000 per month.

Q: Can invoice data be hosted on cloud servers outside the UAE?
A: Yes. Off-shore data storage is permitted provided the electronic records remain completely secure, legible, and instantly retrievable for FTA inspections.
sections.terms_and_conditions:
Phased implementation dates are legally bound by Ministry of Finance revenue brackets; corporate entities bear full liability for disclosing accurate financial data to establish compliance timelines.

The transition phase may require running parallel billing setups, maintaining legacy document distribution for clients not yet integrated into the Peppol network.

Technical failures or ERP downtime preventing XML transmission must be officially reported to the FTA within two business days to safeguard the corporate compliance rating.

This model enables participating families to benefit from shared operational infrastructure, professional investment oversight, and consolidated governance, while each family retains its own distinct wealth structure.

Unlike many offshore alternatives, the ADGM Multi-Family Office operates within a fully onshore international financial centre with access to UAE banking relationships, bilateral investment treaties, and proximity to regional sovereign wealth and family capital. The structure is well-suited to families with diverse asset profiles, including real estate, private equity, listed securities, and digital assets.

sections.introduction:
The ADGM Foundation has established itself as one of the most effective and cost-efficient wealth structuring vehicles available to high-net-worth families and investors in the UAE and across the GCC. Established under the ADGM Foundations Regulations 2017, the ADGM Foundation was the first statutory foundation framework in the UAE, combining the asset-protection characteristics of a trust with the legal personality and structural clarity of a corporate entity.

Unlike a company, an ADGM Foundation has no shareholders. It is a standalone legal entity established by a Founder to hold and manage assets, including shares, real estate interests, bank accounts, investments, and digital assets, for the benefit of designated beneficiaries across one or more generations. The Foundation's governance is set out in two documents: a public Charter that establishes its existence, and private Bylaws that govern how assets are managed and distributed.

One of the most significant advantages of the ADGM Foundation is the privacy it provides. Beneficiary information and distribution rules are recorded only in the private Bylaws, held by the registered agent and not publicly accessible. This, combined with the strong firewall provisions that protect foundation assets from personal creditor claims against the Founder, makes it a compelling vehicle for families seeking asset protection alongside succession certainty.

The ADGM Foundation is frequently paired with an ADGM Restricted Scope Company to hold operating assets, providing an additional layer of confidentiality for the Foundation's business interests. Experienced advisors guide Founders through the preparation of the Charter and Bylaws, KYC submission, and registration with the ADGM Registration Authority, a process that can be completed in as few as three to five working days once documentation is in order.
sections.highlights_and_benefits:
Separate Legal Personality
An ADGM Foundation is a standalone legal entity that owns its assets outright. It can open bank accounts, enter into contracts, and hold property in its own name, without the complexity of a trust relationship.

Strong Asset Protection
ADGM Foundation regulations include statutory firewall provisions that protect Foundation assets from the personal creditors of the Founder, providing robust protection for family wealth once assets are transferred into the Foundation.

Private Beneficiary Information
The Foundation's Bylaws, which set out beneficiaries, distribution rules, and governance mechanics, are held privately with the registered agent and are not accessible to the public or third parties.

Bypass UAE Probate
Assets held by an ADGM Foundation do not form part of the Founder's personal estate. They transfer to beneficiaries according to the Bylaws, bypassing the UAE probate process entirely and avoiding forced-heirship exposure.

RSC Pairing for Operational Assets
ADGM Foundations are frequently paired with a Restricted Scope Company to hold operating assets or business interests, providing a further layer of confidentiality since RSC accounts are not publicly filed.
